title: Add memory discipline guidelines to CLAUDE.md
rationale: mem-agent (HuggingFace, March 2026) formalizes three memory operations: retrieve, update, clarify. The key insight is that RL-trained memory agents learn WHEN NOT TO WRITE — avoiding memory pollution. George's current CLAUDE.md has no guidance on memory update discipline. Adding clear criteria for what deserves to be persisted to MEMORY.md will prevent the file from growing with low-value facts and maintain its utility as a quick-reference document.
content:
## Memory Discipline

Before updating MEMORY.md, apply these criteria:

*Worth persisting (DO write):*
• Facts that will still be relevant in 30 days
• Research findings with specific numbers (Sharpe ratios, win rates, drawdowns)
• Kevin preferences, blockers, and decisions
• System states that affect future scheduled tasks
• Product status and revenue-relevant milestones

*Not worth persisting (DON'T write):*
• Facts already implied by existing entries
• One-time observations with no future relevance
• Information Kevin can re-tell you easily
• Debug details after an issue is resolved

*Memory operations (inspired by mem-agent, 2026):*
1. RETRIEVE — Before answering a question, scan relevant MEMORY.md sections
2. UPDATE — After learning a durable fact, add it with a date stamp
3. CLARIFY — When uncertain whether to store, ask yourself: "Would I need this in 30 days?"
